Planting Prepare the land by ploughing, harrowing and levelling. Provide good perennial shade on the western and southern borders by planting Jack, Neem, Pongamia, Mahagani, Murugula, Silver oak and Causarina. Get pits of size 3 cubic feet dug at a spacing of 9 feet x 9 feet. Fill the pits with top soil mixed with compost. Plant 12 - 18 months aged healthy dwarf seedlings having 5 fronds. Plant seedlings in the centre of the pit 3 inches to 6 inches below the ground level to facilitate watering. Prepare drainage channels at a depth of 2 to 3 feet depth in between 2 rows of arecanut in high rainfall areas.

arhar~sowing.a: Before sowing, the seeds should be treated with sodium molybdate (24 g/acre) with 60 ml of 2% melted jaggery solution as an adhering agent in a plastic container and treated seeds should be dried under shade. Again treat the same seeds bio - fertilizers like with Rhizobium (200 g/acre) and Phosphorus Solubilising Bacteria (PSB) at the rate of 200 g/acre.

Nipping, a practice of removing the tip of the main stem to encourage branching, is typically done in redgram (pigeonpea) at 45 days after sowing (DAS). This timing generally leads to increased branch development and higher yields. Citrus tristeza diseaseDisease symptoms: Disease affected tree leaves becomes chlorotic in the early stages. Gradually the leaves drop and the defoliated twigs show die-back. Diseased trees usually blossom heavily. Under the tree bark stem pitting can be observed. Trees with stem pitting are stunted and set less fruits. The fruits are of smaller size and of poor quality (insipid fruits). Transmission and favourable conditions: The disease is transmitted in semi persistent manner by aphid Aphis gossypii. Aphids are more active in warm summer conditions and increase their population as well as spread of the disease.

cucurbits~sowing.a: Apply Farm Yard Manure or well decomposed cowdung@8-10tonnes per acre.
